notes: Tunis's suburbs: Ariana (the El Ghazala technopark, IT outsourcing), Ben Arous (industrial zones and the Rades container port), Manouba; Tunis-Carthage airport

name: Bizerte
notes: Bizerte (the STIR refinery, Tunisia's only one, and the naval base), the Menzel Bourguiba steel works, Mateur dairy, the Sidi Salem dam

name: Nabeul-Hammamet
notes: Hammamet and Nabeul (beach tourism, pottery), Cap Bon citrus and wine, Zaghouan (the Roman aqueduct's source), the Grombalia industrial zone (wiring harnesses for European cars)

name: Sousse-Monastir
notes: Sousse (tourism, the medina, Tunisia's third city), Monastir (Bourguiba's home, the airport), the Enfidha airport, the Ksar Hellal and Moknine textile and garment factories for Europe

name: Sfax
notes: Sfax (Tunisia's second city and business hub: olive oil exports, the port), the SIAPE phosphate chemical plant, the Kerkennah islands

name: Kairouan-Mahdia
notes: Kairouan (the Great Mosque, carpets), Mahdia (fishing, beaches), the El Jem Roman amphitheatre, olive and almond orchards

name: Gafsa-Tozeur
notes: The Gafsa mining basin (Metlaoui, Redeyef and Moulares: the Compagnie des Phosphates de Gafsa; phosphate has no tag; the 2008 Redeyef protests), the Tozeur and Kebili date palms (deglet nour), the Chott el Djerid

name: Gabes-Djerba
notes: Gabes (the Groupe Chimique's phosphate fertilizer plants, a polluted oasis), Djerba (tourism, the Ghriba synagogue), Zarzis, the Ras Jedir crossing to Libya and its trade, the El Borma oil field and the Tataouine desert (Tunisia's oil and gas south)

name: Kasserine-Sidi Bouzid

name: Beja-Jendouba-Kef
notes: Beja wheat (Tunisia's granary), Jendouba, Tabarka (coral, cork oak forests), Le Kef, Siliana, the Algerian border

name: Algiers Centre-Hydra
notes: Algiers: the government and the El Mouradia presidency, the Bank of Algeria, Sonatrach headquarters at Hydra, the Casbah and the port; Bouteflika was forced out in April 2019 and a successor friendly to Washington was elected in December 2019 (A)

name: Algiers East-Rouiba
notes: Bab Ezzouar (the business district, the USTHB university), Houari Boumediene airport, the Rouiba-Reghaia industrial zone (SNVI trucks, food), Dar El Beida, El Harrach

name: Algiers West-Cheraga
notes: Cheraga, Dely Ibrahim and Ouled Fayet (new offices and villas), Bab El Oued, the Sidi Fredj and Staoueli beaches, Zeralda

name: Blida-Tipaza
notes: Blida (the Mitidja plain's citrus, the Chiffa gorge), Boufarik, Tipaza's Roman ruins, Cherchell (the military academy)

name: Tizi Ouzou-Boumerdes
notes: Kabylie: Tizi Ouzou (Berber culture, the 2001 Black Spring, emigrants in France), Boumerdes (the Algerian Petroleum Institute), olive oil, the Azazga forests

name: Bejaia-Bouira
notes: Bejaia (the port and oil terminal at the end of the Hassi Messaoud pipeline, Cevital's sugar and oil empire), the Akbou agro-food valley, Bouira and Lakhdaria

name: Setif-Bordj Bou Arreridj
notes: Setif (the high plateaus' commercial city, wheat), Bordj Bou Arreridj (Condor and the other electronics assemblers, Algeria's electronics capital), the El Eulma wholesale market

name: Constantine
notes: Constantine (the city of bridges over the Rhumel gorge, the east's capital, universities), the Ain Smara industrial zone, the Ali Mendjeli new town, the Mila farms and the Beni Haroun dam

name: Annaba
notes: Annaba (the port, the El Hadjar steel works, ArcelorMittal's until 2016 and state-owned since), Guelma, El Tarf (El Kala national park, the Tunisian border)

name: Skikda
notes: Skikda (the LNG plant rebuilt after the 2004 blast, the Skikda refinery and petrochemicals), Jijel (the Bellara steel plant with Qatar), cork forests

name: Batna-Khenchela
notes: Batna (the Aures mountains, the Chaoui Berbers, where the 1954 revolution began), Khenchela, the Timgad Roman city, cement

name: Tebessa-Ouenza
notes: The Ouenza and Boukhadra iron ore mines (feeding El Hadjar), the Djebel Onk phosphate (phosphate has no tag), Tebessa, Souk Ahras, Oum El Bouaghi; smuggling across the Tunisian border

name: Biskra-El Oued
notes: Biskra (deglet nour dates), El Oued (the Souf: potato farms in the desert, the town of a thousand domes)

name: Msila-Bou Saada
notes: M'Sila, Bou Saada (the gate of the desert), steppe sheep farming, the Hodna salt lake

name: Oran
notes: Oran (Algeria's second city, rai music, the port, Es Senia airport), the Hassi Ameur industrial zone, the Renault Symbol plant at Oued Tlelat (2014)

name: Arzew-Bethioua
notes: Arzew and Bethioua (Algeria's main LNG trains, the Arzew refinery, ammonia and methanol plants, Sonatrach's industrial zone)

name: Mostaganem-Relizane
notes: Mostaganem (a port, colonial-era vineyards), Relizane (the Chelif valley farms)

name: Tlemcen
notes: Tlemcen (the Zianid capital, Andalusian heritage), Maghnia on the Moroccan border (closed since 1994, fuel smuggling), Ghazaouet port, Beni Saf (the Medgaz pipeline to Spain), Ain Temouchent

name: Sidi Bel Abbes-Mascara
notes: Sidi Bel Abbes (the old Foreign Legion town, the ENIE electronics plant), Mascara (Emir Abdelkader's home, wine and cereals), Saida

name: Chlef-Ain Defla
notes: Chlef (cement, the 1980 earthquake), Ain Defla and Tissemsilt; the Chelif valley farms

name: Medea-Djelfa
notes: Medea (the Atlas foothills, vineyards), Djelfa (sheep on the steppe, Algeria's livestock capital), Ksar El Boukhari

name: Laghouat-Hassi R'Mel
notes: Hassi R'Mel (Algeria's largest gas field since 1961, the hub of the Transmed pipeline to Italy and the Medgaz pipeline to Spain), Laghouat, Tiaret (horses, wheat on the high plateaus)

name: Hassi Messaoud
notes: Hassi Messaoud (Algeria's largest oil field since 1956: the Sonatrach base and foreign oil company camps, a restricted zone), the pipelines north to Arzew, Bejaia and Skikda

name: Ouargla-Touggourt
notes: Ouargla (the oil region's city), Touggourt, the Oued Righ date palms, the Haoud Berkaoui oil fields

name: Ghardaia
notes: The M'zab valley (the Ibadi Mozabite merchants, a UNESCO site), Ghardaia, Metlili; Mozabite-Arab clashes in 2013 to 2015

name: Illizi-In Amenas
notes: In Amenas (the Tiguentourine gas plant of BP, Equinor and Sonatrach, attacked by Islamists in January 2013), Illizi, the Tassili n'Ajjer rock art, the Libyan border

name: Tamanrasset-In Salah
notes: In Salah gas (BP, Equinor, Sonatrach), Tamanrasset (the Hoggar mountains, the Tuareg, trade with Niger and Mali), the southern military command

name: Adrar-Timimoun
notes: Adrar, Timimoun and Reggane (the Touat and Gourara oases, the French nuclear test sites of 1960), the new Touat gas fields

name: Bechar-Tindouf
notes: Bechar (the army's western command, the closed Kenadsa coal mines), Tindouf (the Polisario Front's refugee camps and the seat of the Sahrawi republic in exile), the undeveloped Gara Djebilet iron ore, the Naama and El Bayadh steppe

name: Casablanca Centre-Anfa
notes: Casablanca: the Casablanca Finance City towers, the Casablanca Stock Exchange, the Attijariwafa bank and OCP headquarters, Anfa, the Hassan II mosque, the port of Casablanca (Morocco's biggest general port)

name: Casablanca East-Mohammedia
notes: The Ain Sebaa and Sidi Bernoussi industrial zones, Mohammedia (the Samir refinery, idle since 2015, and the oil port), Mohammed V airport at Nouaceur and the Midparc aerospace suppliers

name: El Jadida-Jorf Lasfar
notes: Jorf Lasfar (OCP's phosphate chemical hub, the world's largest phosphate fertilizer complex, and the Jorf Lasfar coal power plant), El Jadida (the Portuguese citadel), the Doukkala farms

name: Settat-Berrechid
notes: Settat, Berrechid (an industrial zone: auto parts), Benslimane; Chaouia wheat

name: Rabat-Sale
notes: Rabat (the capital: the Royal Palace and the makhzen, parliament, Bank Al-Maghrib, ministries, embassies), Sale, Temara, the Technopolis offshoring park

name: Kenitra
notes: Kenitra (the Atlantic Free Zone and the PSA Peugeot plant, opened in 2019), the Gharb plain farms (sugar, rice, citrus), Sidi Kacem, Khemisset

name: Tangier-Tanger Med
notes: Tangier (the old international zone), Tanger Med (Africa's largest container port, on the Strait of Gibraltar), the Renault Melloussa plant (Africa's largest car factory), the Tanger Automotive City and free zones, the Al Boraq high-speed train to Casablanca (2018)

name: Tetouan-Fnideq
notes: Tetouan (the Andalusian medina), the Martil and M'diq beaches, Fnideq and the border with Spanish Ceuta (smuggling porters), Larache and Ksar El Kebir; Morocco claims Ceuta (note only)

name: Al Hoceima-Rif
notes: Al Hoceima (the 2016 to 2017 Hirak Rif protests), Chefchaouen (the blue town), Ouazzane, the Rif mountains' cannabis farms

name: Oujda-Nador
notes: Oujda (on the Algerian border, closed since 1994), Nador (the border with Spanish Melilla, which Morocco claims (note only); the Nador West Med port under construction), Berkane citrus, the closed Jerada coal mines (protests in 2018), Figuig

name: Fes
notes: Fes (the medina, Al Quaraouiyine university, the tanneries, the spiritual capital), Sefrou, Taounate

name: Meknes-Ifrane
notes: Meknes (the imperial city, the wine and olives of the Saiss plain), Ifrane (Al Akhawayn university), El Hajeb, the Azrou cedar forests of the Middle Atlas

name: Marrakech
notes: Marrakech (Jemaa el-Fnaa, riads and the tourism boom), Al Haouz and the High Atlas, the Kelaat Sraghna olives, Ben Guerir (OCP's new university and phosphate mines)

name: Safi-Essaouira
notes: Safi (Morocco's sardine port, OCP's phosphoric acid plants, pottery), Essaouira (the Gnawa festival, argan oil), the Youssoufia phosphate mines (phosphate has no tag)

name: Khouribga-Beni Mellal
notes: Khouribga (OCP's largest phosphate mines on the world's biggest reserve; phosphate has no tag), Beni Mellal (the Tadla plain: sugar beet, citrus), Khenifra, Fquih Ben Salah

name: Agadir-Souss
notes: Agadir (the sardine fleet, Morocco's biggest fishing port, beach tourism), the Souss valley's export tomatoes and citrus, Taroudant, Tiznit, the argan forests

name: Ouarzazate-Errachidia
notes: Ouarzazate (the Noor solar complex, one of the world's largest, and the film studios), the Imiter silver mine near Tinghir (Managem, Africa's largest), Errachidia, the Draa and Ziz oases (dates)

name: Guelmim-Tan Tan
notes: Guelmim (the camel market, the gate of the desert), the Tan-Tan fishing port, Sidi Ifni; the region borders Western Sahara

name: Laayoune-Boujdour
notes: Laayoune (Morocco's administrative capital for Western Sahara, the UN MINURSO mission), the Bou Craa phosphate mine and its conveyor to the coast (phosphate has no tag), Boujdour and Tarfaya; the berm separates the Moroccan-held west from the Polisario-held strip to the east

name: Dakhla
notes: Dakhla (octopus and sardine fishing, kitesurfing, greenhouse tomatoes), Aousserd, the Guerguerat crossing to Mauritania
